VERY IMPORTANT





































DO NOT review other AIA member’s books. Amazon knows that you are somehow connected. 
** Please read amazon/kdp TOS in regards to what you can/cannot review
*** This does not apply to ACX (Audible) While exchanging positive reviews is not allowed - it is perfectly fine to review other publishers books - so long as you are leaving an honest review.
Support

Q: Why can’t I access the next module in the course?
A: The modules are unlocked 1 week at a time to ensure that students don’t skip steps in the publishing process and also so that students have a complete understanding of the material before moving on. To unlock a modle, you must complete the previous “end of module assessment” and click “done” on all lessons.

Check out this video to watch it: http://tinyurl.com/y5yq34

Q: I’m an existing member, and the weeks have been locked again, how do I access the course again from where I left off?
A: There was a pretty extensive overhaul and redesign of the entire course recently, so yes your weeks are “locked” again. But all you need to do is the same process listed above. Just click “done” and the following week will unlock. (you may need to hit refresh for the change/unlock to take effect) if you’ve tried this several times and it’s not working - please email help@courseplatform.com

Q: I am having trouble logging in, where is the login page?
A: https://app.publishinglife.com/products/audiobook-income-academy-2-0

Q: Do you have an affiliate program?
A: No, not at this moment. Our affiliate program is closed until further notice.

Q: How do I get a refund?
A: Please send an email to help@courseplatform.com where you will be prompted to fill out a refund request form.

Q: How many coaching calls do I get included with my membership? 
A: 4, and they are set up to be scheduled at the end of weeks 2 - 5.
If you can’t make it to your coaching call: please reach out to help@courseplatform.com to let us know. Try to cancel/reschedule 24 hours prior to your call. Life happens - just reach out and let us know what’s up! 

Q: Can I purchase extra coaching calls?
A: No, not at this time. 

Q: How do I change my password for AIA access? 
A: At the top left of the AIA dashboard you click the link for “Programs”. On the top right of the “Programs” page - you will see  your profile pic/avatar - click that and open “Profile Settings” - From there, you can change your password. 

Resources

Q: Where do I access all of the resources in the course?
A: A list of all of the resources that are covered in the course can be found in the AIA 2.0 Resource Cheatsheet

Q: How do I request access to edit the AIA docs and resources?
A: You don’t. You will be making a copy of each doc and resource. To do this: go to file > make a copy.























LLC and Taxes

Q: If I am from the US, do I need to set up an LLC?
A: No. You can just publish as an individual using your social security number aka your tax id number. You don’t need to worry about opening up an LLC until you are making good profit (5k+ per month) from your business, where at that point it would become tax beneficial for you to open an LLC.

The same applies if you have a tax ID number from Canada, UK or Ireland.

Q: If I am not from the US, UK, Canda, or Ireland, do I need to set up an LLC?
A: You do not need to open an LLC to publish ebooks and print books on KDP no matter where in the world you are from. Previously students would set up an LLC if they wanted to publish audiobooks on ACX, but this has been usurped by ACX who now require proof of residency in the US, UK, Canada or Ireland. 

If you are outside of those 4 countries, you can still publish your audiobooks without an LLC, just not with ACX. You would need to use a 3rd party distributor such as Author’s Republic. They will still get your audiobooks published on Audible, the disadvantage is that you will not receive the promo codes that ACX gives (which are very helpful for gaining reviews) and you will receive a smaller royalty percentage. This is why ACX is preferred for those who can access it. There is a lesson specifically for getting your book on Audible via Authors Republic in module 6 lesson number 10 ‘Authors Republic’

Q: How do I handle taxes for my LLC?
A: All tax information should be directed to a certified tax professional. Information on where to find an online-business CPA can be found on page 31 of the Resource Cheatsheet.










Topic Research
ATTENTION: CHROME EXTENSIONS WILL NOT WORK ON MOBILE DEVICES
LESSON UPDATE: DO ALL RESEARCH IN “BOOKS” STORE ON AMAZON

Q: I am having trouble getting the keyword/Topic research extensions (DS Quick View, KDSpy) to work, how can I fix this?
A: 
Step 1 - You need to ensure that you are running the programs in incognito mode on your browser. To do this you need to: Click the menu button in chrome > More tools > Extensions > click ‘more info’ on the extension > Allow in incognito
Step 2 - Clear all cookies and cache history on your browser
Step 3 - Restart your computer
KDSPY support: https://www.publishingaltitude.com/contact-us/


Q: I am having trouble finding the topic tracker and the profit analyzer spreadsheets, where can I access them?
A: The topic tracker and profit analyzer spreadsheets are the same Google Slides file. You can find all parts of the topic tracker spreadsheet on the bottom tab of the file. The file is linked under lesson 5 in module 2 or you can download it HERE. Note - all of the downloadable files can be found in the Resources Cheatsheet and in the description of each lesson.

Q: Should I do keyword research on books that I write myself?
A: You should still apply the same principles that you learned in the SLEEK modules to analyze competition. The goal is to write books that are in low competition niches with a small amount of search results. Remember that you most likely won’t be building an audience with these books. They are intended to generate cash flow, not become the foundation of your business. Refer to module 3 lesson 8 for details.

Q: Do I need to do a trademark search for the keywords I choose for my books?
A: Yes. Everytime you use a keyword for a book you need to do a trademark search. We show step-by-step how to do a trademark search in this lesson.

Q: When I am doing keyword research, should it be on Amazon.com or their other marketplaces?
A: All keyword research should be done on Amazon.com.

Q: Should I get KDROI?
A: No, it isn’t effective anymore
Pen Name(s)

Q: How many pen names can I create?
A: You can create an unlimited number of pen names.

Q: How many pen names can I have per Author Central account?
A: Each Author Central account can have three pen names. So, if you have fifteen pen names, you'd still only have one Amazon account, but five Author Central accounts, each with three pen names.

Q: How do I create my pen name’s bio (what can/can’t I say about my pen name)?
A: You cannot lie about your pen name’s credentials or expertise. Calling yourself an up-and-coming writer in your niche with passion to help others in that area is a great start. You do not need to have 20 years experience in a field for readers to trust your word. If the information inside your book is great, that is more than enough for them to view you as an authority on the topic. Any other credentials you can apply on top of that is the cherry on top.

Publishing Life Services has an “Amazon Author Bio Package” if you would like a professional to write your author bio for you: https://services.publishinglife.com/products/amazon-author-bio-package

Q: What gender should my pen name be?
A: Your pen name can be the same gender as the majority of your target audience. Keep in mind that your pen name’s gender is an insignificant factor to your publishing business’s success.

Q: How do I create a pen name? 
A: It ultimately matters not. Pick a name, any name— you can literally make it up! As long as it follows general naming principles in line with the place/culture that your pen name “comes from” you are good to go! 
great examples: John Wilkins, Patti Monroe, Leslie Doyle, Stefan Belanger






Q: Can I use a brand name as my pen name?
A: Yes, absolutely that is a great idea if that’s what you would like to do. The advantages are that you can easily hire many different writers without readers noticing a different writing style in your books because they understand it is likely multiple writers that write all the books. A disadvantage is that some readers would rather read books from an individual person rather than a brand name because there’s a more personal connection.

There is no right or wrong in the pen name vs brand name discussion, it is a matter of personal preference. In the end, it will have a very small impact on your business.

Q: Should my narrator be the same gender as my pen name?
A: Ultimately— your narrator’s style should fit the theme of your book.

Q: Should I join facebook groups with my pen name’s facebook page or on my personal account?
A: Facebook has recently limited the abilities of facebook pages. You can’t direct message anyone in other facebook groups as your page and groups can also limit if pages are allowed to join or not. Therefore, you will be limited to the amount of groups you can join and what you can do inside of those groups. For this reason it is recommended that you contact people using your personal facebook account. People will not be suspicious about your name not matching your pen name as long as you are upfront that you write using a pen name.

Q: Whose face can I use for my pen name?
A: You can use royalty free images. Additionally you can use something like This Person Does Not Exist to get unique, AI generated images. Refer to the Resource Cheatsheet for a list of stock photo sites. 


Ghostwriters

Q: What is the best ghostwriting company?
A: The Urban Writers and Hot Ghost  are the most reputable ghostwriting companies. Keep in mind, the writing quality will be dependent on the specific writer that you get, not the company itself. 

Q: What do I do if I am not happy with the quality of the manuscript I received?
A: Communicate with the writer/ghostwriting company. Ghostwriting companies are typically very understanding. Mark the revisions that you would like to see as clearly as possible and explicitly state what needs to be changed. Simply saying, “the writing is bad and needs to be better” isn’t going to yield the result you are looking for. Always keep in mind that you will always get further with kindness than anger.

Q: How can I ensure that the manuscript I receive is as high-quality as possible? 
A: You need to have as clear and effective of an outline as possible. That means articulating your thoughts clearly and doing high quality research. Always be sure to make your communication to your ghostwriter extremely clear.

Q: I’ve contacted support and my issues still weren’t solved with my manuscript, what do I do?
A: Only escalate your issue if it is absolutely necessary and if you are sure that you did everything in your power to make the order come out the way you would like. If you need to escalate an issue, you can ask to speak with a supervisor at the company and in a worst case scenario you can request a refund. Exercise your ability to request a refund cautiously and sparingly. You don’t want to ruin your relationship with any ghostwriting company. If you are using The Urban Writers and find yourself in an EXTREME situation with your order and you’re not receiving the support that you would like; the owner, David Silva, is a part of the AIA facebook community and has been known to solve community member’s EXTREME problems in the past. Note - DO NOT MESSAGE DAVID SILVA FOR REGULAR SUPPORT PROBLEMS. Exercise the privilege to communicate to The Urban Writers owner very selectively.  



Q: How do I hire ghostwriter’s from Upwork?
A: Watch module 3 Lesson 7 to learn everything you need to know about ghostwriter’s from Upwork. 

Q: Where can I find a copy of the ghostwriter agreement contract?
A: It can be found HERE. Remember that all resources can be found in the Resource Cheatsheet. 

Q: The Urban Writer’s premium package seems like a great deal for everything that is offered, should I go with it even if it is my first time producing a book?
A: No. You should learn every step of the process before you begin outsourcing them all. That means learning how to research, develop an outline, craft a description, conceptualize a book cover, etc.

Q: Is there a significant difference between the top tier and the lower tier writers?
A: Sometimes there is and sometimes there isn’t. It depends on which writer you are given. Many people find that the price difference isn’t worth the difference in quality. Remember, the most important factor to you getting the book you want is your communication with the writer. Ultimately, it is your responsibility to get the book where it needs to be before you publish. 

Q: Do I need to proofread and edit the book if ghostwriting companies offer it in the package?
A: Yes. You always need to read your books before you publish them. No one has more incentive to create a high quality book than you do. Therefore, you are going to be the best person to know what the book needs to be like for your audience and what problems need to be fixed.

Q: Can I write books myself?
A: Yes watch module 3 lesson 8 for a complete step-by-step guide. 

Q: Is there a discount code for Urban Writers and Hot Ghost Writer?
A: Try TWINS5 as this was a valid discount code most recently for both platforms.

Book Content

Q: Can I write summaries of other successful books?
A: No. You will be infringing on copyright and trademark laws. 

Q: Can I publish works that are now in the Public Domain or PLR content?
A: No. This is a violation of Amazon’s Terms of Service and will result in account termination and possible banning from KDP.

Q: I need custom illustrations/designs for my book. How do I hire a designer?
A: You can find designers on Fiverr, Upwork, and 99Designs. Simply tell them what you need and negotiate a price for the job. 

Q: How can I make sure my book isn’t plagiarized?
A: Make sure that your book is thoroughly cited. Always run a plagiarism check on your books before you publish them. Plagiarism checkers will never be 100% accurate. Anything between 2-5% is acceptable. Be sure to check back and see what was marked as plagiarized content, it may just be poor citing or an error with the plagiarism checker. This will help you to determine what the true plagiarism amount is. 

Q: What is the overall cost of publishing a book?
A: Please refer to module 2 lesson 9 for a more detailed breakdown. 

Q: How do I create a copyright page in my book?
A: The AIA copyright template can be found here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mBs3xvH6NSlLyvWJIchgcjGtVmQwOruMG-Nmq_yrIEo/edit?usp=sharing 

Q: Where do I get images for my book?
A: The images must be royalty free and “free for commercial use”. You can get them from stock photo sites like shutterstock and pixabay







Q: How do I cite sources in my book? 
A: The most common style is APA style. You can choose whatever style you like, as long as you are consistent throughout your book. (ex: Chicago Style, AMA, MLA etc) This is a great automatic APA citation generator: https://www.scribbr.com/apa-citation-generator/
If you’d like a simple “style guide” here is a massive reference explaining all about APA style.  
https://www.mendeley.com/guides/apa-citation-guide

Q: How do I register for copyright protection for my book?
A: Read this informative blog article on the subject: https://blog.reedsy.com/how-to-copyright-a-book/
Here is a link to the US Copyright registration site: https://copyright.gov/registration

A new lesson was created in April 2022 which helps walk you through the process, this can be found in module 5 lesson 7





















Book Covers

Q: What is the best option if I want a high quality cover?
A: Please refer to module 2 lesson 9 to know what your options are in relation to your budget. Also refer to the Resource Cheatsheet for a complete list of options.

Q: How do I know if my book cover is good or not?
A: See module 3 lesson 9 for everything you need to know on cover design.

Q: Can I put a ‘bestseller’ tag on my book cover?
A: Yes, but only if it has actually achieved ‘bestseller’ status on Amazon.

Q: KDP is giving me an error code when I try to upload my book cover, what do I do?
A: Contact your cover designer and let them know what the error message was that KDP sent (it will always tell you how to fix the problem) as well as a screenshot of the error page. It is your cover designer’s responsibility to deliver the correct size.

Q: When do I begin the cover design process?
A: You can start the book cover design process as soon as you have decided on your title. Be aware that you will need to know the final page count for your paperback book before your spine and back cover can be made.

Q: How many characters can I have in my title/subtitle?
A: 200, including spaces and punctuation.

Formatting

Q: What size should my book be?
A: Your book size is entirely up to you. Common sizes are 5x8, 5.5x8.5 and 6x9. Keep in mind that larger dimensions will result in a smaller page count. Your dimensions should reflect the theme of your book. For example, children's workbooks would probably be better suited with larger dimensions and a general non-fiction book about Business & Money would be better suited for more standard dimensions. 

Q: How do I format my book?
A: Module 5 lesson 2 has all of the information you need. As always, be sure to check the lesson description for links and additional information.

Q: I’m not good with coding, how can I format my Book Description?
A: Here is a free online book description html code generator. Just put in your text, format in the edit window how you want it to look, then the generator generates the code for you! 
https://kindlepreneur.com/amazon-book-description-generator/

Q: Can I /should I print my book(s) in color?
A: No. At least not on KDP, and not without a massive increase in retail price. The cost to print color on KDP is astronomical and does not lend itself to a very good profit margin therefore is not recommended. We recommend printing in Black and White ONLY. (please see print cost estimator in the next question)

Q: Where can I find an Amazon printing cost estimate calculator?
A:  https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G200735480#royalty_calculator








Bundles

Q: What is a bundle?
A: Everything you need to know about bundles is covered in Week 7 Lesson 3. Be sure to check the lesson description for additional information.

Q: Can I bundle a book more than once?
A: No.

Q: Do I launch bundles the same way as single books?
A: Yes.

*Please note - Amazon/KDP changes it’s listing requirements from time to time.
They are no longer accepting the word “bundle” for paperback books. You can use it for ebooks and audiobooks - but paperback will not get approved. Therefore we recommend using compilation, collection, compendium, anthology, treasury or digest.






















ACX

Q: ACX is taking forever to approve my audiobook. What do I do?
A: Have patience. ACX has increased their time estimates for the audiobook review process. If your book is past a 90 business day timeframe, contact ACX customer support. The phone support team is usually more helpful than the email support.

Q: ACX told me that there are errors in the audio files of my book, what do I do?
A: ACX also notified the narrator. Follow up with the narrator and let them know what the problem is and ensure that they fix the problem. 

Q: How do I cancel a contract with my narrator?
A: Contact ACX support and they will do it for you.

Q: Should I stay exclusive with ACX or go wide with other distributors?
A: You should stay exclusive with ACX. Audible has by far the largest market share of any audiobook platform. 

Q: Do I get paid for redeemed promo codes?
A: No.

Q: How do I generate more promo codes?
A: Go to the promo codes tab on the sale’s dashboard and click the button that says ‘get promo codes’. Next, scroll to the bottom and click ‘request more promo codes’. Note - Once your book has achieved 10 Promo Code redemptions and has made 100 qualified sales across your catalog you may request 25 more codes, up to 50 per title per marketplace.

Q: How do I pay the narrator?
A: Usually PayPal. Classify your payment as “for a business or service” so that there is payment protection in the event that a problem arises. (but you can also use wise,payoneer or whatever other online payment processor you both agree to)


Q: How do I send the finished manuscript to the narrator?
A: You will send them your finished manuscript through ACX’s website. Follow the prompts on the audiobook production page once you have signed a contract with a narrator.
KDP

Q: How do I upload my book to KDP?
A: Sign into your KDP account, go to your ‘bookshelf’, and follow the prompts under ‘create a new title’.

Q: If I have an issue with my KDP dashboard, receiving a payment, or one of my books, what do I do?
A: Contact KDP support.

Q: Should I enroll in KDP Select?
A: Yes, this is discussed in the launch lesson of week 5. You should enroll in KDP Select because it allows you to run “free book promotions” and “kindle countdown deals” that you can utilize to launch your book. There is also an invisible hand effect that occurs when you are enrolled in KDP Select. This means that your book is shown to more people. The exclusivity agreement is only applicable to your ebook, not the paperback. You can continue to publish your paperback(s) through other distributors if you are enrolled in KDP Select. 

Once your launch phase is complete you should then opt out of KDP Select so that you can distribute your book on other platforms. You MUST opt out before distributing elsewhere…
















Extras, Codes etc.

Q: What is the current code for publishing with Ingram Spark?
A: We can not guarantee that this code will work, but we will try to keep it updated to the most current version of the code. Best thing to do if this code doesn’t work is to contact Ingram Spark directly, or use google. 

This is the latest offer from Ingram Spark - note, this was the same code offered throughout March so it is worth trying this if there are no other codes available…

Want to upload a completely new title to your IngramSpark account? Take advantage of up to five free title setups by using promo code: FREEFIVE22. (*Offer expires April 30, 2022. Code must be applied at the time of title setup. Not valid on previous titles. Good for up to 5 titles per account. Cannot be used with free ISBNs).

AIA Extra Membership: has to be applied for under the Bonuses section on the course website. You’ll find it in the bonuses section by clicking the word ‘bonuses’ at the top of your AIA dashboard home page: ‘Extra AIA Membership’, please fill out that form. Applications are processed by hand. Please allow up to 5 business days for approval. If you haven’t heard back after that time please email: help@courseplatform.com

Extra Membership Limitations:
IMPORTANT: You may gift your bonus membership to ONE person, and one person ONLY. You may not change your mind later, shift to another person, or share with more than one individual.

Extra bonus memberships have full and lifetime access to the core course content. (Provided the original member remains in the AIA program & does not opt for a refund.)
Extra memberships however, are limited on some of the bonus material, and DO NOT have access to:
1:1 coaching
Recorded Q&A calls (they can still access the live calls
Certain bonus lessons
Access to the FB community. 
Extra membership access DOES include: 
Guaranteed Profits Workshop
Top 100 Proven Niches
10K Case Studies Vault
The Social Media Accelerator Course
Weekly Live Q & A Calls

Q: Where can I find the AIA Merch Store? 
A: https://shop.publishinglife.com

Q: Where can I find the Amazon Advertising Standards of Practice to know if my topic/keyword/book will be allowed to be advertised on the platform? 
A: https://advertising.amazon.com/resources/ad-policy/book-ads 
Section 3.3 specifically relates to prohibited book content. 

Q: Why can’t my reviewer leave a review on Amazon? 
A: There might be many reasons why. Amazon has a strict minimum spend for any account. To be in good standing, typically, accounts have to have spent at a minimum $50 USD on physical products (not ebooks) in the last 6 months to leave reviews on products. Other than that Amazon reserves the right to cancel/suspend any reviewer’s account for any reason. This is entirely out of your control, and has nothing to do with AIA - there is nothing we can do either. So please carry on, get more reviewers. Like all things - just keep going. 






















Glossary of Terms

A 
AIA [X.xx] - Audio Book Income Academy [version number of the course]
ABSR: Average Best Sellers Rank (see also, BSR)
Acknowledgments: A section of your book dedicated to recognising and honouring the people who may have influenced the book, its publishing, or who might have made a difference to the life of the author.
ACoS: Advertising Cost of Sales - Simply put, this is how much you spend on Amazon advertising in order to generate $1 in revenue from that spend. Similar to Google's Return on Ad Spend (ROAS), ACoS is a great metric for PPC marketers to see if advertising campaigns are profitable. (see also PPC)
ACX - Audio Creation Exchange is where publishers and narrators come together to produce audiobooks.
AI: Artificial Intelligence
AI Algorithm: Artificial Intelligence Algorithm takes a combination of both – inputs and outputs simultaneously in order to “learn” the data and produce outputs when given new inputs. (see also algorithm)
Algorithm: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined, computer-implementable instructions, typically to solve a class of specific problems or to perform computations.
AMZ - Shortened version of “Amazon”
App: Abbreviation for “application”, usually an app performs a specific function on desktop or mobile devices
Appendix: The part of a book that contains supplemental material, such as tables, references, or extra information. It is usually placed at the end of the book.
ARC: Advance Reader Copy, usually sent out ahead of book launches to reviewers.
ASIN: Amazon’s own version of an ISBN- Amazon Specific Identification Number
Author Copy: A copy/copies of a book sent to the author for preview/review to check and approve for final printing, not meant for retail sale. (see also proof)




B
Backlist: An author or publisher’s older and sometimes out-of-print titles.
Back Matter: The counterpart of front matter. This means material such as appendices, notes, references, glossaries, bibliographies, or indexes. These are placed at the end of the book. (see also front matter)
Bar Code: Common on many retail products - an image made up of lines which encodes a book’s ISBN/ASIN. Normally printed on the back cover of a book. Essential to bookshops when selling or tracking books.
Binding: The format into which a print book is assembled. Binding types range from case binding, spiral binding, and perfect binding (this is what AMZ POD uses).
Bleed: Printing that goes beyond the Trim Size of a page.
Blurb: The brief description of the book, used for marketing purposes. Can be found on the back of a paperback or on the inside flap of a hardcover. 
Book fair: An exhibition and convention for publishers, authors, or booksellers.
Book proof: A proof is the preliminary, often uncorrected, iteration of a book, intended for a limited audience, such as reviewers. (See author copy/review copy).
Book trailer: A video advertisement for a book, much the same as a film trailer.
Brand: A name, term, design, symbol or any other feature(s) that identify one seller’s goods/services from that of other sellers. 
BSR: Best Seller Rank - Amazon’s way of showing how well your book is selling. The lower the number = the more copies you are selling. 
Bundle: 2 or more paperbacks, ebooks or audiobooks sold together as a collection/compendium compiled into 1 product. 

C
Case bound: A type of binding and the industry term for a book in hardback/hardcover format.
Conversion: See Formatting.
Copyright: The exclusive right to make copies, license, and otherwise exploit a literary, musical, or artistic work, whether it be printed, audio, or video. Works are protected for the lifetime of the author or creator, and for a period of 50-75 years (depending on the country) after his or her death.
Copy editor: An editor employed to work on the detail of a book, focusing on accuracy, style and also consistency of formatting, punctuation, and layout.
Copywriting: The act of writing “copy” - words specifically for the purposes of marketing/selling a product. 
Colophon: Originally this term referred to the bibliographic information printed at the end of a book, the term is now used almost exclusively for the device or logo of the book’s publisher or author.
Cover spread: The entire cover of a physical book, from the front, including the spine, to the back.
 
D
Dedication: Part of the front matter that dedicates a book to a specific person, place, or thing.
Developmental Editor: An editor who focuses on the overall organisation of a book’s content rather than the wording of sentences. A developmental editor is also responsible for re-ordering entire blocks of text, entire chapters, or the re-structuring of a book's plot. The editor may also address tone, voice, addition or deletion of material, complexity of material and transitions between paragraphs or sections of the book.
Distribution: Making your book available to wholesalers, retailers and readers.
Distributor: A company that distributes books to retailers, occupying the gap between authors/publishers and the retailer.
Domain: An Internet domain name consists of a series of alphanumeric segments, separated by full stops, complying with Internet standards, typically “masked” or converted to a simple to read URL. (see also URL)
Dust jacket: A detachable outer cover that protects the book, printed with the cover design. Usually for hardback/hardcover books.
 
E
eBook: The electronic version of a book, usually read on dedicated eReading devices such as Kindle or Kobo readers, or on devices such as smartphones, tablets, or PCs.
EBITDA: A company’s Earnings Before Interest Taxes Depreciation and Amortization are subtracted- acts as a proxy for a company’s current operating profitability.
Edition: A specific version of a text.
Endorsement: A written statement promoting an author or their book. Usually placed on the cover or in the front matter of the book.
Email List: A list of customers/potential customer’s emails- collected, curated for the purposes of contact, marketing and sales generation (see also lead magnet and funnel)
Email Sequence: Series of emails sent to your leads (see funnel)
ePub: A very popular file format, used mostly by retailers other than Amazon, such as
iBooks, Kobo, and Barnes and Noble.
Exclusivity: In traditional terminology, this is part of a publishing contract which binds the author solely to one publisher. In the self-publishing industry, it means being exclusive to one particular store or retailer.
 

F
FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions - usually a document containing all of the most frequently asked questions for a particular course, group, community etc. Often in list style format. Learning Resource (see also: this entire document) 
FB: common acronym used for FaceBook, the social networking app
Fiverr: a website for finding freelancers to outsource very small/short-term projects such as graphics conversion, small layout changes, sometimes book cover design
Formatting: The process of turning a manuscript file (like a Word document) into a format that can be published as an eBook or published by a POD printer.
Freelancer: or freelance worker. A term usually used for a person who is self-employed and not necessarily committed to a particular employer or project, long-term. Typically hired for smaller projects (see also outsourcing, upwork, fiverr, gig)
Front list: Traditional terminology meaning books in their first year of publication.
Front Matter: Any material preceding the beginning chapters of the book. This could be the table of contents, the dedication, the acknowledgements, introduction, and foreword.
Funnel: Sometimes also called a sales funnel, is a consumer-focused marketing model that illustrates the theoretical customer journey toward the purchase of a good or service. (see also lead magnet, lead, and email list)
 
G
Galley: The interior text of a book after all the editing and formatting has been done.
Genre: A category denoted by the content of a book, such as fantasy, romance, horror, or non-fiction 
Ghostwriter: A writer who writes books, articles and stories that are credited to another person. Celebrities often use ghostwriters for autobiographies and magazine articles.
Gig: typically referred to by freelancers as a short term project or job
GPW: Guaranteed Profits Workshop - a workshop/bonus designed as proof of concept and to enact an action taking mindset. Not meant as a complete publishing guide, and does not include paperback formatting/audio book or full design instructions etc.  
GW: Ghost Writer, one who ghost-writes a book - usually a freelancer
Greyscale: An image solely composed of black and white.
Guerilla Marketing: Sometimes also referred to as “Roots Marketing” Often IRL tactics to market your books, typically not requiring money, but requiring time or “sweat equity” to put boots on the ground and talk to people face to face and do “traditional” in person marketing. (see also IRL, roots marketing)

H
Hard Return: Pressing the enter or return key at the end of a line of text instead of allowing the text to naturally move to the next line.
Hardback/Hardcover: A book that simply has a hard cover, rather than a paper cover
HGW: Hot Ghost Writer, a ghostwriting company


I
IG: Instagram, popular image sharing social network, owned by FB
Imprint: An Imprint can refer to the name of a publisher, or a division or subsection of a publishing house that specialises in certain subjects or genres.
Impressions: This is the number of times your ad is shown to potential buyers, and does not count the number of times your ad is actually clicked. (see also ppc and ACos)
Incognito Mode: Private browsing is a privacy feature in some web browsers. When operating in such a mode, the browser creates a temporary session that is isolated from the browser’s main session user data. This allows you to access a website, like Amazon, with a “clean slate” for research purposes. (see also VPN)
Independent Press: A small publishing company whose annual revenues are below a certain level. These levels may change from country to country, or even among regions in the same country. (see also Small Press)
Index: Like a table contents, an index directs readers to specific subject matter in the book.
Influencer: a person/organization on social media with a following/fanbase generally larger than 100,000 people
Interior: All the content within the book. Refers to everything except the cover.
Interior graphics/images: Pictures, diagrams, figures and other items that appear within the interior of a book.
International Standard Book Number (ISBN): A unique 13-digit number (can be 10 or 13 digits if issued prior to 2007) that identifies a specific edition of a book or eBook. UK authors can procure batches of ISBNS from the UK ISBN agency Neilsen. US authors must purchase ISBNs from Bowker, the US equivalent. In Canada these are registered and distributed by the Canadian Government.
IP Address: Internet Protocol Address is a unique string of characters that identifies each computer connected to the internet and communicates over that network (see also VPN)
IRL: In Real Life (internet term, coined to differentiate between cyberspace and real life)
IS: Ingram Spark - a separate POD service from Amazon, best for hardback, color or bulk orders.
 
J
Jacket: The paper cover wrapped around a hardback.
 
K
Keyword: An important word or phrase that can be assigned to a book on platforms such as KDP, used by search engines and readers looking for genres, authors, or certain types of books.
Kindle: An eReader produced by Amazon.
KDP: Kindle Direct Publishing- A platform provided by Amazon to authors. KDP allows authors to publish eBooks directly to all Amazon stores, via a very simple dashboard.
KDSPY: A program used for keyword analysis, showing average BSRs, Sales, Reviews and other important data.
Kobo: Another major retailer based in Canada and owned by the Japanese company Rakuten. They have a very wide and profitable global market, and also provide their own range of eReaders.
 
L
LCK: Low Content Kickstarter bonus in the AIA course for creation of small, fast, low-cost audio books. Designed to help get cashflow happening relatively quickly/easily. Not meant as a complete publishing guide, and does not include ebook/paperback formatting/full design etc.  
Lead: A sales term used to define a person who is/may be interested in your offer.
Lead Magnet: Something valuable that entices potential leads to join your email list/funnel (see also email list and funnel)
Limited Edition: A book printed in limited numbers, usually for special editions.
Line Editor: An editor who performs an edit that is heavier than the usual copyedit and who focusses on a book's voice, tone, or phrasing. Fictional line editors focus on the story's pacing, character development, minor details and vocabulary of the period and place where the story is set. They will also focus on the effectiveness of dialogue. A line editor also focuses on correcting errors in grammar, punctuation and writing style.
List Price: The recommended retail price of a book. Set by the author or publisher and often referred to as the RRP, or recommended retail price.
Literary Agent: A person or company responsible for looking after the interests of authors. Literary agents manage the exploitation of rights in an author’s work. They handle the submission of manuscripts to traditional publishers, negotiate contracts, and collect monies due.
LLC: Limited Liability Corporation. A legal entity, setup for taxation purposes on US soil. Not needed nor available in UK/Canada/Ireland. May be necessary for citizens outside of these regions to have in order to conduct business with ACX/KDP 
 

M
Manuscript: The complete version of the book before any editing or formatting.
Marketing: Promotional and advertising activity to sell books. Sometimes paid, sometimes free/cheap.
Metadata: The data about a book. At its very simplest, metadata are: title, author, publisher, price. 
Mobi: Amazon’s own eBook format, exclusive to Amazon. For use on Kindle devices and apps.
 
N
Nook: A brand of eReader developed by Barnes & Noble.
Niche: A subset of the market on which a specific book (or series of books) is focused. The niche defines the book topic(s) aimed at satisfying specific market needs by solving specific market problems. This can also be used to speak about the demographic the book is intended to target. 

O
Offset Printing: Printing technology where ink is transferred from a roller to a printing surface, and then to a page of a book. Used for large print runs. A more traditional form of printing, compared with modern digital techniques. Often combined with lithography, which is based on the principle of repulsion between oil and water.
Outline: A document that is an entire framework or blueprint which describes and provides all the resources for your ghost writer to write your book from. 
Outsourcing: Practice of finding and hiring freelancers to complete tasks/projects for your business that you do not have time or the professional experience to complete on your own.
 


P
P&L: An income statement or profit and loss account is one of the financial statements of a company and shows the company’s revenues and expenses during a particular period
PDF (Portable Document Format): A popular file format type produced by Adobe Systems that is widely used. All formatting and style is preserved within the file. Although eBooks can and are produced in PDF, the format is not as widely used as Mobi or ePub formats.
Perfect bound: A type of binding where a glue/adhesive attaches the pages at the spine. Usually with a paper cover, hence the more-common name ‘paperback’.
PFH: Per Finished Hour. Standard measurement of how narration is paid for
PLS: Publishing Life Services
PPC: Pay-per-click is an internet advertising model used to drive traffic to websites or products where an advertiser pays when an ad is clicked. While generally more expensive per click - the trade off is more highly targeted “warm” leads. (see also impressions, ACos)
PPM: Pay-per-mille (mille is latin for 1000). This is the opposite of PPC, where instead of paying for more specialized leads - you are paying for the impressions overall, in this case a flat fee for 1000 impressions. This is more in line with “traditional” marketing. If you have a highly engaging and converting ad - this type of ad may be cheaper. (see also PPC, ACos, impressions)
Print run: The number of copies printed in a single order.
Print-on-Demand (POD): A publishing process in which books are printed only when orders are placed. This bypasses and therefore removes the cost of warehousing.
Proof: A copy of the book, manuscript, or cover produced so that it can be checked by the publisher or author. (see also author copy)
Proofreader: An editor who is employed to read through proofs to check accuracy and formatting.
Publication Date: The official date from which a book is available to the public.
Publicist: A person who generates and manages media and public attention for a book through writing press releases, arranging events, book signings, author interviews and book reviews.
 

Q
QA: Stands for Quality Assurance
Q&A: Stands for Question & Answer. AIA hosts several weekly Q&A zoom meetings for members to join and learn/ask questions live. While not necessary, and not part of the core course - they are an excellent addition to your learning and can be a great chance to connect, virtually, with your course mates/fellow students.  

R
Return: A return is a book that either fails to sell or has become damaged, and is returned to the author or publisher.
Review: A published opinion provided by a professional or amateur book reviewer or reader. (see also social proof)
Review copies: Books that are provided to reviewers by the publisher or author, usually ahead of the release. See Book Proof.
Review Count: The number of reviews your book has in either a single market or across all markets.
ROI: Return on Investment is the ratio between net income and investment. A high ROI means that the investment’s gains compare favourably to it’s cost. As a performance metric, ROI is used to evaluate the efficiency of an investment or to compare the efficiencies of several different investments.
Roots Marketing: see Guerilla Marketing
Royalty: A percentage of the book’s sale price that is paid to the author. Royalties are paid to authors based on the sales of their books. Publishers will undertake a contract with their authors outlining what the Royalties for book sales will be. Amazon also pays a Royalty to you the author/publisher. Royalties are treated differently than sales, and therefore do not require you to have a taxation number in most territories/countries. 
RRP: Recommended Retail Price See List Price.
 

S
Self-Publishing: A form of publishing that bypasses the traditional model of publishing, employing eBook publishing platforms, POD printers, and various other DIY techniques to reach readers and markets directly, bypassing the need for a traditional “publisher”.
SEO: Search Engine Optimization, commonly refers to the act of optimizing a web page, blogpost, social media post for indexing by the large internet search companies - specifically Google
SLEEK: The method taught by AIA to find profitable keywords. Stands for Scrape, List, Examine, Eliminate, Keyword selection
Slush pile: The ‘pile’ of unsolicited manuscripts that are sent to publishers and agents. Often not read.
Small Press: (See Independent Press) A small publishing company whose annual revenues are below a certain level. These levels may change from country to country, or even among regions in the same country. 
Social Proof: On Amazon this is commonly known as review count, it establishes how much the market at large likes/dislikes your book usually displayed in stars. (see also review/review count)
Spine: The thin section between the back and front covers, usually reserved for the title, author name and publisher/author logo.
Spiral-bound: When wire or plastic is spiralled through holes punched along the binding side of a book.
SWANH: Star Wars, A New Hope - the only Star Wars that matters
 

T
Table of Contents: This section appears in a book's front matter. It lists a book's chapters and their page numbers.
Target Audience: A specific group of readers or a section of the market for whom the book is aimed at.
Territory: Where book rights are concerned, authors and publishers can license and own different rights in different countries or continents. As an indie author, we usually retain exclusive worldwide rights.
TOC: Table of Contents
Trade discount: See Wholesale Discount.
Trade Mark: ™ A trademark is a type of intellectual property consisting of a recognizable sign, design, brand name, or expression which identifies products. Sometimes also identified and/or accompanied by the ® symbol. 
Trim size: The dimensions of a print book, specifically the page size.
TUW: The Urban Writers, a ghost writing company
Typesetting: To arrange the interior of the book in such a way so that it is print-ready. Also referred to as formatting, specifically print formatting.
 
 
U
Unit Cost: The production or base cost of printing and putting together a book.
USD: US Dollars, common payment denomination when dealing with freelancers (see also freelancer)
URL: A Uniform Resource Locator, colloquially termed a web address (think of www.website.com) is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism to retrieve it. A URL is actually a very specific type of Uniform Resource Identifier, although most people use the two terms interchangeably. (see also domain)
UW: Short form for UpWork, a website for finding freelancers to outsource larger one-off projects like ghostwriting or book design/layout (see also freelancer)
 

V
Vanity Press: Traditionally, a Vanity Press was seen as a business or organisation which produced books at the author’s expense.
VPN: Virtual Private Network extends a private network across a public network (the internet) and enables users to send and receive data from a shared access point, or network as if their computers were directly connected to a private network that is outside of the prying eyes of the world wide web. VPNs can be extremely useful for masking IP addresses and for research purposes where you do not want data to be used to show you “targeted” data, or if it is required for your computer to appear as if it is logging onto the web from a specific geographical location. (see also IP address)

W
Wholesale discount: The reduced price at which retailers or distributors buy books from authors or publishers.

Y
YT: YouTube, popular video sharing social network, owned by “Alphabet” a division of Google


Z

ZPE: Zero Point Energy- energy released in Quantum Torpedoes

Based on the Q&A document you provided, here are the most important points regarding designs, writing summaries, using the same summary, and getting traction for your books on KDP.

### 1. Designs (Book Covers)

The "Book Covers" section of the Q&A provides the following key guidelines:

*   **Quality & Options:** For high-quality cover options, refer to **module 2, lesson 9** and the **Resource Cheatsheet**.
*   **Evaluating a Cover:** To know if your book cover is good, see **module 3, lesson 9**.
*   **Bestseller Tag:** You can put a ‘bestseller’ tag on your cover, but **only if the book has actually achieved bestseller status** on Amazon.
*   **Upload Errors:** If KDP gives an error when uploading your cover, contact your designer. Provide them with the error message and a screenshot. It is the designer's responsibility to deliver the correct size.
*   **Design Process:** You can start the cover design process as soon as you have decided on your title. For paperbacks, you will need the final page count to create the spine and back cover.
*   **Title Length:** Your title and subtitle can have a maximum of **200 characters**, including spaces and punctuation.

### 2. Writing Summaries

The document has a critical warning about writing summaries in the "Book Content" section:

*   **Do Not Summarize Other Books:** You **cannot** write summaries of other successful books. The Q&A explicitly states, "No. You will be infringing on copyright and trademark laws." Doing so violates Amazon’s Terms of Service and can result in account termination.

When creating your own book description (which serves as a summary or "blurb"), the document suggests:
*   Use a free online HTML generator to format your book description nicely. The link provided is: `https://kindlepreneur.com/amazon-book-description-generator/`.
*   The glossary defines a "Blurb" as the brief description used for marketing, found on the back of a paperback or online.

### 3. Using the Same Summary for Multiple Books

The Q&A does not explicitly state whether you can use the same summary for three similar books. However, based on the overall guidance, it is strongly advised **against** doing so.

*   The core philosophy of the course is to create unique products for low-competition niches.
*   Using the same or very similar summaries could be flagged by Amazon as duplicate content, which would hurt your book's visibility and ranking.
*   The document emphasizes tailoring your book to a specific niche and audience. Each book, even if similar, should have its own unique angle and description to attract buyers. You should write a unique description for each book.

### 4. Getting More Traction for Your Books

The document offers several strategies for gaining traction, primarily in the "KDP" and "Extras" sections, as well as the glossary.

*   **Enroll in KDP Select:** During your book launch, you should enroll in KDP Select. It allows you to run “free book promotions” and “kindle countdown deals.” The Q&A mentions there is an "invisible hand effect" that increases your book's visibility. After the launch phase, you should opt-out to distribute your book elsewhere.
*   **Generate Reviews (Social Proof):** Reviews are crucial. The glossary defines "Social Proof" as your review count and star rating. You can generate promo codes (via ACX for audiobooks, or other methods) to give away to readers in exchange for honest reviews.
*   **Create Bundles:** Sell 2 or more books together as a collection. For paperbacks, avoid using the word "bundle" in the title; use words like "compilation," "collection," or "anthology" instead.
*   **Marketing:** The glossary highlights several marketing concepts:
    *   **Guerilla/Roots Marketing:** In-person, low-cost tactics.
    *   **Email List/Funnel:** Build a list of potential customers and engage them with a series of emails.
    *   **SEO:** Optimize your book's keywords and description.
*   **Advertising:** The document links to Amazon's Advertising Standards of Practice (`https://advertising.amazon.com/resources/ad-policy/book-ads`) and mentions PPC (Pay-Per-Click) advertising metrics like ACoS.
*   **Understand Your Audience:** Use tools like the "Customer Research Worksheet" provided at the end of the document to deeply understand your target reader's desires, frustrations, and goals. This is the foundation of effective marketing.

In summary, focus on creating original content, designing a professional cover, writing unique descriptions for each book, and actively marketing your work through KDP promotions, bundling, and building an audience.

based on the lesson plan can you provide for me a viable action plan using steps to create my own books?

Of course. Based on the lesson plan and Q&A document you provided, here is a viable action plan with steps to create your own books for platforms like KDP.

### Action Plan: Creating and Publishing Your Own Book

This plan follows the structure and recommendations laid out in the Audio Book Income Academy (AIA) course materials.

#### Phase 1: Research and Planning

1.  **Choose a Niche and Topic:**
    *   Use the **SLEEK method** (Scrape, List, Examine, Eliminate, Keyword selection) taught in the course to find profitable keywords.
    *   Conduct all keyword research in the **"BOOKS" store on Amazon.com**.
    *   Analyze competition. Aim for low-competition niches with a small amount of search results. These books are for generating cash flow, not necessarily building an audience (refer to **Module 3, Lesson 8**).
    *   Perform a **trademark search** for your chosen keywords. A step-by-step guide is provided in the course.

2.  **Define Your Target Audience:**
    *   Complete a **Customer Research Worksheet** (like the one provided at the end of the document) to understand your ideal reader's demographics, frustrations, desires, and goals. This is crucial for writing and marketing.

3.  **Set Up Your Business Framework (Optional but Recommended):**
    *   As an individual, you can publish using your Social Security Number or Tax ID. You do not need an LLC unless you are making over $5k/month.
    *   Create one or more **pen names**. You can create an unlimited number. Each Author Central account can hold up to three pen names.

#### Phase 2: Content Creation

4.  **Write the Book (Choose One Path):**
    *   **Path A: Write It Yourself.**
        *   Watch **Module 3, Lesson 8** for a complete step-by-step guide.
    *   **Path B: Hire a Ghostwriter.**
        *   Use reputable companies like **The Urban Writers** or **Hot Ghost**.
        *   First, learn the entire process yourself before outsourcing everything.
        *   Develop a clear and detailed outline.
        *   Use the provided **ghostwriter agreement contract** (found in the resources).
        *   Communicate clearly and kindly with the writer. If revisions are needed, mark them clearly.
        *   Consider using a discount code like **TWINS5**.

5.  **Create the Book's Content:**
    *   **Do not** write summaries of other books (copyright infringement).
    *   **Do not** use Public Domain or PLR content (violates Amazon TOS).
    *   Include a **copyright page** using the AIA template (link provided in the Q&A).
    *   Use **royalty-free images** ("free for commercial use") for any illustrations. Get them from sites like Shutterstock or Pixabay.
    *   Properly cite your sources (APA style is suggested, but be consistent). Use an automatic citation generator if needed.

#### Phase 3: Production and Design

6.  **Design the Book Cover:**
    *   Decide on your title first.
    *   Refer to **Module 2, Lesson 9** and the **Resource Cheatsheet** for cover options and budgeting.
    *   See **Module 3, Lesson 9** for guidance on evaluating a good cover.
    *   Start the design process early. For paperbacks, you'll need the final page count for the spine.
    *   Keep your title and subtitle under **200 characters**.
    *   Use royalty-free images or an AI generator like "This Person Does Not Exist."

7.  **Format the Book Interior:**
    *   Choose a book size (e.g., 5x8, 5.5x8.5, 6x9). Dimensions should fit the book's theme.
    *   Format the manuscript for both eBook and paperback. Instructions are in **Module 5, Lesson 2**.
    *   Use the free **HTML generator** for your book description: `https://kindlepreneur.com/amazon-book-description-generator/`.
    *   For paperbacks, print in **black and white only** to maintain a good profit margin.
    *   Estimate printing costs with the **KDP calculator**: `https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G200735480#royalty_calculator`.

#### Phase 4: Publishing

8.  **Publish on KDP (eBooks and Paperbacks):**
    *   Sign into your KDP account, go to your bookshelf, and follow the prompts to create a new title.
    *   During your launch phase, **enroll in KDP Select**. This allows you to run free promotions and countdown deals. Opt-out after the launch to distribute elsewhere.
    *   If you encounter issues, contact KDP support.

9.  **Publish on ACX (Audiobooks - if eligible):**
    *   Eligibility requires proof of residency in the US, UK, Canada, or Ireland.
    *   Find a narrator on ACX, The Urban Writers, Hot Ghost, or Upwork.
    *   Send the finished manuscript to the narrator through the ACX website after signing a contract.
    *   Pay the narrator (usually via PayPal, classified as a business service).
    *   Be patient with the approval process. Contact ACX support if it exceeds 90 business days.
    *   Stay exclusive with ACX for the largest market share.
    *   Generate promo codes to encourage reviews (after meeting certain sales thresholds).

#### Phase 5: Launch and Marketing

10. **Launch Strategy:**
    *   Utilize your **KDP Select** enrollment to run a launch promotion (e.g., free book days).
    *   Consider creating a **bundle** (2+ books sold together). For paperbacks, use terms like "compilation" or "collection" instead of "bundle."

11. **Gain Traction and Reviews:**
    *   Build an **email list** and use a sales funnel with an email sequence.
    *   Engage in **Guerilla Marketing** (in-person, low-cost tactics).
    *   Consider **Amazon PPC advertising** (understand metrics like ACoS and Impressions).
    *   Generate promo codes (from ACX or other methods) to give to readers in exchange for **honest reviews**.
    *   **Important:** Do not review other AIA members' books. You can review other publishers' books honestly.

By following these steps, you can systematically create, publish, and launch your own books based on the principles outlined in the course.
